newsitem.title: GERMANY: German farm sector wants EU milk quota extension.
newsitem.headline: German farm sector wants EU milk quota extension.

text.p: The German farm ministry and farm union DBV on Wednesday urged the extension of the European Union milk quota system beyond the year 2000.
A DBV presidium meeting on Tuesday, which said while the current system needed reforming, the EU would not agree to a liberalisation of production volumes.
"We must not abandon volume restrictions because of the special conditions under which we operate in Europe," said a statement issued after the meeting..
An independent report last month called for abolition of the system ahead of the next round of world farm trade talks starting in 1999 and EU enlargement eastwards.
Member states in favour of extension say production must not be allowed to shift to a few centres at the cost of extensive dairy farming across the EU as this may cause social problems.

German farm minister Jochen Borchert said Brussels should set export rebates and subsidies boosting producer prices while maintaining the quotas, which had proved to be the best instrument over the past 12 years.
EU farmers could not produce at costs close to world market levels and needed protection because their incomes were threatened.
The Commission is due to present dairy reform proposals early next year.
